AGENTS.md — using sdmTMBexperiments with an AI assistant

Source: AGENTS.md

This file is written for AI assistants helping a user use sdmTMBexperiments to run experiments on fitted sdmTMB models. For working on the package source itself, see CLAUDE.md.

What this package does

sdmTMBexperiments is a collection of experimental helper functions built around fitted sdmTMB models: model comparison, mesh-resolution sensitivity, retrospective analysis, survey-specific index comparison, prediction-grid construction, and diagnostic/result plotting. Functions are generic (nothing is hard-coded to a species or region) and may later be adopted into sdmTMB itself. Cite the developer when you reuse them.

Maps are drawn on ggOceanMaps basemaps, which is the package’s default map-plotting tool.

Core conventions

  • Coordinates: model X/Y are expected in kilometres (the sdmTMB convention). Helpers multiply by coord_multiplier (default 1000) to get CRS metres for sf/mapping.
  • Attach the package with library(sdmTMBexperiments) — this attaches ggOceanMaps (a Depends) so basemaps find their bundled land data.
  • Suggested packages some functions need: concaveman (survey regions), blockCV (sdmTMB_mesh_cv()), inlabru (plot_mesh()), DHARMa, ggspatial (bubble_map()), cli (progress messages).

Minimal working examples

library(sdmTMBexperiments)
library(sdmTMB)

mesh <- make_mesh(pcod, c("X", "Y"), cutoff = 20)
m1 <- sdmTMB(density ~ 0 + as.factor(year), data = pcod,
             time = "year", mesh = mesh, family = tweedie())
m2 <- sdmTMB(density ~ 0 + as.factor(year) + depth_scaled, data = pcod,
             time = "year", mesh = mesh, family = tweedie())
nd <- replicate_df(qcs_grid, "year", unique(pcod$year))

# Compare models (indices + spatial prediction differences + Mohn's rho)
cmp <- compare_models(m1, m2, newdata = nd, object_crs = 32609)
plot(cmp)                     # index time series
plot(cmp, type = "spatial")   # per-cell prediction-difference maps

# Mesh-resolution sensitivity
mc <- compare_meshes(m1, mesh_cutoffs = c(10, 30), newdata = nd,
                     reference_name = "20 km")
plot(mc)

# Retrospective analysis
retr <- sdmTMB_retro(m1, nd, nyears = 5)
plot(retr)

# Diagnostics and result maps
plot_mesh(mesh, crs = 32609, data = pcod, value = "density")
pred <- predict(m1, newdata = nd)
plot_prediction_map(pred, crs = 32609)          # averaged density
plot_random_field(pred, crs = 32609, field = "omega")
plot_residual_qq(m1)
plot_variance_partitioning(m1)

Model selection

sdmTMB_selection() fits a named list of candidates to identical records and returns a tidy, defensible selection table. The same function covers every selection stage — component ranking, dropping fixed effects, family, spatiotemporal structure, mesh resolution — because each is the same operation with a different thing varied.

cands <- list(
  "Full model"        = density ~ 0 + as.factor(year) + depth_scaled,
  "No depth"          = density ~ 0 + as.factor(year),
  "No spatiotemporal" = list(spatiotemporal = "off"),
  "Tweedie"           = list(family = tweedie()),
  "Coarser mesh"      = list(cutoff = 40)
)

sel <- sdmTMB_selection(
  cands, data = pcod,
  formula = density ~ 0 + as.factor(year) + depth_scaled,
  cutoff = 25, family = tweedie(), time = "year",
  spatial = "on", spatiotemporal = "iid",
  cache_dir = "data/output/selection"      # one file per candidate, resumable
)

sel                                  # print method: the table + comparability
plot(sel)                            # status-coded ranking dot plot
plot(sel, type = "index", newdata = nd)   # does the choice move the index?
best_candidate(sel)                  # by the metric column, never by row order

Cross-validate a shortlist, not the whole ladder — CV costs k fits per candidate:

short <- best_candidate(sel, n = 3, by = "aic")
cv <- sdmTMB_selection(cands[short], data = pcod, ..., cv = 10,
                       cache_dir = "data/output/selection")

Rules that make the table mean something (all enforced or reported by the function; see ?sdmTMB_selection):

  • Candidates are fitted to identical records (complete_cases = TRUE, via selection_frame()). Fit the selected specification to the full data afterwards.
  • Compare only rows with comparable == TRUE, and never quote a delta between two candidates unless both are.
  • Hold-out log-likelihood is reported per observation, with n_heldout and folds_pdhess beside it.
  • fold_ids from blockCV::cv_spatial() gives spatially clustered folds (extrapolation into unsampled ground); the default random folds measure interpolation. lfo = TRUE scores prediction of unseen years, which is what an assessment update actually asks.

Survey comparison (uses the bundled sebastes data)

compare_surveys() fits a separate model per survey series, builds a survey-specific prediction grid from each survey’s spatial footprint, and compares to a compiled reference index.

data(sebastes)
region <- make_survey_prediction_region(subset(sebastes, cruiseseries == "EggaN"),
                                        crs = 32633)
grid <- make_prediction_grid(region, resolution = 20)

Common pitfalls

  1. X/Y are in km. Passing metres will place data in the wrong location.
  2. Attach, don’t just ::. Map functions rely on ggOceanMaps being attached (it is, via library(sdmTMBexperiments)). Using :: on a bare namespace can fail with object 'dd_land' not found.
  3. Bias correction is slow. bias_correct = FALSE is the default; turn it on only for final runs.
  4. compare_surveys(type = "spatial") needs a compiled_model; without one, spatial differences are skipped.
  5. Do not read the selected model off the first table row. Use best_candidate(); the sort key changes with whether cross-validation ran.
  6. A sanity = FALSE winner is not disqualified. sanity() fails routinely on usable fits, so it does not gate comparable — read it as a reason to consider simplifying, not as a row to skip.

For agents developing the package

If you are helping work on the package source (not just using it), start with CLAUDE.md and the memory/ folder. memory/ is the project’s persistent memory; memory/MEMORY.md is the index.

Bump the version with every commit. Increase Version in DESCRIPTION (by default one patch step per commit; minor/major only when the maintainer asks), set Date to the commit date, and give NEWS.md a matching # sdmTMBexperiments x.y.z heading. See memory/versioning.md.

Do not put personal information into memory/, AGENTS.md, or CLAUDE.md. The whole repository is public on GitHub. Never commit absolute local paths (e.g. /Users/<name>/...), machine-specific filenames, or contact details beyond the maintainer’s public package metadata; use placeholders such as ~/... or path/to/your/file.
